s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent unilateral neck cellulitis with associated temporal bone anomalies and fistula
salient_findings: Unilateral otomandibular syndrome with severe temporal bone hypoplasia
Discharge through the artificial ear canal during episodes of cellulitis
Fistula originating from the middle ear
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 40s
History of unilateral otomandibular syndrome
Severe temporal bone hypoplasia
Multiple mandibular and auricular reconstruction surgeries in childhood
First episode of neck cellulitis occurred in 2014
Second episode of neck cellulitis occurred in 2021
Discharge through the artificial ear canal during the second episode
Recurrence of neck cellulitis two months after the second episode
Imaging studies showed collection in the right parapharyngeal space and neck
Hypodense lesion noted in the middle ear on initial CT scan
Fistula originating from the middle ear on follow-up MRI
2-centimeter mass found during drilling of the hypoplastic petrous bone
Millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid running into the sternocleidomastoid muscle

shortlist.label: First branchial cleft anomaly
shortlist.why_kept: Associated with recurrent neck cellulitis and temporal bone anomalies

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: Middle ear mass and fistula are consistent with cholesteatoma complications

shortlist.label: Temporal bone osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe temporal bone hypoplasia and recurrent infections suggest chronic osteomyelitis

shortlist.label: Mastoiditis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the mastoid bone is consistent with the patient's symptoms and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Fistula of the middle ear
shortlist.why_kept: Directly observed on imaging studies and consistent with the patient's discharge through the artificial ear canal

raw.rationale: The patient's history of unilateral otomandibular syndrome, severe temporal bone hypoplasia, and recurrent neck cellulitis with discharge through the artificial ear canal, along with imaging findings of a fistula originating from the middle ear and a millimetric fistula at the tip of the mastoid, are consistent with a first branchial cleft anomaly.

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma
rejected.why: While cholesteatoma could explain the middle ear findings, it does not fully account for the patient's history of unilateral otomandibular syndrome and severe temporal bone hypoplasia.

rejected.label: Temporal bone osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis could be a complication of the patient's condition, but it does not explain the underlying cause of the recurrent neck cellulitis and fistulae.

rejected.label: Mastoiditis
rejected.why: Mastoiditis is a possible complication, but the patient's symptoms and imaging findings suggest a more complex congenital anomaly.

rejected.label: Fistula of the middle ear
rejected.why: While a fistula of the middle ear is present, it is likely a component of the larger congenital anomaly, rather than the primary diagnosis itself.
